entry.title: Hotfix Daily #2: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Claude Duet, Flint and more
entry.summary: Hotfix Daily #2: MiniMax M3.1 Flash pricing, Anthropic's Claude Duet agent, Recursive's local Flint coding model, AI at Steam Next Fest, and OPAL.
entry.content:
Read this issue on the web · Sponsor Hotfix Daily

MODEL

1 MiniMax ships M3.1 Flash at $0.15 per million input tokens

MiniMax says its new Flash model runs agent tasks nearly 3x faster and about 70% cheaper than its predecessor, with a 1M-token context. Pricing is flat: $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output. Weights are promised later.

Why builders care: If you tried the free :free variant on OpenRouter, it ends today at 12:00 UTC (7 AM CT). Switch to the base slug minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash so nothing breaks.

Source

AGENTS

2 Anthropic previews Claude Duet, an agent that comes to you first

Duet is a separate app (iOS, Android, claude.ai) that checks your connected apps every few hours, sends a morning brief, and keeps working on its own cloud computer after you close it. It asks for approval before it sends, pays, signs, or deletes anything. It's waitlist-only for US Pro and Max users.

Why builders care: Its background checks count against your plan's usage limits, which is a useful model for how to budget an always-on agent of your own.

Source

CODING

3 Recursive's Flint: a coding model that runs on your laptop

Flint is a 40B mixture-of-experts model that uses about 2.5B parameters per token. Recursive reports 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified and more than 125 tokens/sec on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro. It's Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and works with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM.

Why builders care: A private, offline coding agent with no usage bill. Compare it with the hosted options in our coding agent guide.

Source

GAME DEV

4 More than a third of Steam Next Fest games now use generative AI

TheGamer's count of SteamDB data found 2,595 of the 7,145 games in October's Next Fest (over 36%) carry Steam's AI tag, up from just over 19% in June. Players are pushing back, and many of the top-charting demos are AI-free.

Why builders care: Disclosed AI use is now normal on Steam, and players are watching. Being clear about how you used it can help you stand out.

Source

REPO

5 Repo of the day: OPAL, an optimizer an agent rewrites mid-training

From MIT researchers: wrap your PyTorch optimizer in one line, and a coding agent (Claude Code by default) watches the run and rewrites the update rule, schedules, and loss-spike guards as it trains. MIT-licensed, with a cost cap you set.

Why builders care: For a new task with no tuned recipe, the authors report it matches or beats the best off-the-shelf recipe across their image and language tests.

Source

Hotfix of the Day

Match reasoning effort to the step. On MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, effort defaults to max if you leave it out. Set it to low for routing, classification, and simple tool calls, and keep high or max for planning and debugging. Check what your provider defaults to.

Source

entry.title: Hotfix Daily #1: Mercury 3, Voxtral 3, Beacon and more
entry.summary: Hotfix Daily #1: Inception's Mercury 3, Mistral's Voxtral 3 voice agent SDK, Beacon shared agent memory, AI in game studios, and Google's Harness².
entry.content:
Read this issue on the web · Sponsor Hotfix Daily

MODEL

1 Inception ships Mercury 3, a diffusion model built for speed

Mercury 3 drafts the whole response at once and then refines it, instead of writing one token at a time. On Inception's own benchmarks it beat GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on 8 of 12 tests at 1,068 tokens/sec, and it has a 1M-token context. No one outside the company has published results yet.

Why builders care: It is on OpenRouter and Vercel, and OpenAI-API code needs only minor changes, so testing it is cheap.

Source

AGENTS

2 Mistral launches Voxtral 3 and a voice agent SDK

New speech-to-text and text-to-speech models plus an SDK built on LiveKit. It runs listening, reasoning, tool calls, and speech as one streaming pipeline, and Mistral says each turn finishes in under a second. It works over WebRTC in browsers and over SIP for phone calls.

Why builders care: Voice agents used to mean wiring three vendors together. Now it's one SDK priced per minute, and you can still swap out the LLM.

Source

CODING

3 Beacon: shared memory for your coding agents

Asymptote Labs raised a $5.5M seed round for Beacon, an MIT-licensed open-source layer. It records sessions across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and 20+ other agent tools, and it lets lessons from earlier sessions carry over instead of disappearing.

Why builders care: If you hop between Cursor and Claude Code, you can stop re-explaining your project to each one.

Source

GAME DEV

4 Game studios use AI everywhere, but not deeply

Vivrato interviewed 101 studio leaders: 94% use AI in at least one production stage, yet 52% rate how deeply it's built into their pipeline at 3/10 or lower. European studios reported deeper adoption than North American ones.

Why builders care: The gap is in the pipeline. Studios have picked up AI tools but haven't built them into how they work, and that's an opening for tools that fit real game dev workflows.

Source

REPO

5 Repo of the day: Google's Harness²

This trending open-source framework (Apache 2.0) improves the setup around an agent while the agent works: prompts, memory, tools, skills, and subagents. The model itself stays the same. Google reports gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench. It supports OpenCode and Codex as executors.

Why builders care: You can get better results by improving the setup around your model, without switching to a new one.

Source

Hotfix of the Day

Before you accept "done" from your coding agent, make it show proof: run the tests, the build, or a screenshot. Then have a fresh-context subagent review the diff. The Claude Code team says that's the first layer of their review process. From June to September, their merged PRs more than doubled while the share needing reverts fell by over 40%. Put your run-able checks in a short CLAUDE.md (or .cursorrules).

Source
